question.text: Consider the vector $\mathbf{u}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ \sqrt{k} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Given that $\mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v}=-10$ and $\Vert \mathbf{v}\Vert =2$, what is the smallest possible value of $k?$
question.explanation:
We will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,

\[ \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert \leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert. \]

We are given all the quantities in the inequality above, except for $\Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert.$ So first, we compute $\Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert$ as follows:

\begin{align*} \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert &=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+(\sqrt{k})^2+1^2}\\[3pt] &=\sqrt{14+k} \end{align*}

Now, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have \begin{align*} \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert & \leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[3pt] \vert -10 \vert & \leq \sqrt{14+k}\cdot (2)\\[3pt] 5 & \leq \sqrt{14+k} \\[3pt] 5^2 & \leq \left(\sqrt{14+k}\right)^2\\[3pt] 25 & \leq 14+k \\[3pt] 11 & \leq k. \end{align*}

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $k$ is $11.$

question.text: Consider the vector $\mathbf{u}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ \sqrt{k} \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Given that $\mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v}=16$ and $\Vert \mathbf{v}\Vert =4$, what is the smallest possible value of $k?$
question.explanation:
We will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,

\[ \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert \leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert. \]

We are given all the quantities in the inequality above, except for $\Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert.$ So first, we compute $\Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert$ as follows:

\begin{align*} \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert &=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+(\sqrt{k})^2+(-1)^2} \\[3pt] &=\sqrt{k+6} \end{align*}

Now, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

\begin{align*} \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert & \leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[3pt] \vert 16 \vert & \leq \sqrt{k+6}\cdot (4)\\[3pt] 4 & \leq \sqrt{k+6} \\[3pt] 4^2 & \leq \big(\sqrt{k+6}\big)^2 \\[3pt] 16 & \leq k+6 \\[3pt] 10 & \leq k. \end{align*}

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $k$ is $10.$
